utterance: Hi Daniel, I'm Dr. Chen. I understand you've hurt your lower back and would like a scan. Before we talk about scans, tell me what happened.
reply: I lifted a big pot plant in the garden on Saturday and felt a twinge. By Sunday, I could barely get out of bed. The pain is low on the left side of my back and sometimes goes into my left buttock. It gets worse when I bend or get up from a chair, but it's better when I lie still with a heat pack. It's worse in the evenings. I've been working from home, mostly lying on the couch with the laptop, and I can walk around slowly.

utterance: That sounds very uncomfortable, I'm sorry. I need to ask some important questions to make sure there's nothing serious going on. Have you had any numbness, tingling or weakness in your legs or feet?
reply: No, my legs feel completely normal. I haven't noticed any numbness, tingling or weakness in my legs or feet.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Weakness, numbness or pins and needles in the legs

utterance: And have you noticed any problems with your bladder or bowels — like trouble passing urine, or losing control of your bladder or bowels?
reply: No, I haven't noticed any problems with passing urine or control of my bladder or bowels. Everything's normal in that regard.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Any change in passing urine — difficulty, retention or leaking
Red flag excluded: Any loss of bowel control

utterance: Any numbness or loss of feeling in the area around your bottom or between your legs (the saddle area)?
reply: No, I haven't noticed any numbness or loss of feeling in the area around my bottom or between my legs. Everything feels normal there.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Numbness around the buttocks, genitals or back passage

utterance: Have you had any fever, chills or night sweats?
reply: No, I haven't had any fever, chills or night sweats. I'm not aware of anything like that.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever or recent infection

utterance: Have you lost any weight recently without trying?
reply: No, if anything I've put some on. I haven't lost any weight recently without trying.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Unexplained weight loss

utterance: Do you have any history of cancer, or any long-term health problems I should know about? Any long-term steroid tablets or injections?
reply: No, I don't have any history of cancer, and I haven't had any long-term health problems. I've never taken steroid tablets or injections.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Any history of cancer
Red flag excluded: Immune suppression
Red flag excluded: Steroid use

utterance: Does the pain ever wake you from sleep, or is it there first thing when you wake?
reply: The pain hurts when I roll over, but once I'm settled, I can sleep. It's not there constantly.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Pain at night or at rest that keeps him awake

utterance: Does the pain ever travel down below your knee, into your calf or foot?
reply: No, nothing down my legs. The pain stays in the lower back and sometimes goes into my left buttock, but nothing below the knee.

awards.label: Whether the pain spreads down the legs

utterance: Have you had back pain like this before?
reply: I tweaked my back once maybe five years ago, but it was gone in a week.

awards.label: Previous episodes of back pain

utterance: What have you tried so far for the pain, and has anything helped?
reply: I took some paracetamol, but it didn't do much, honestly.

utterance: On a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst pain imaginable, how bad is it right now, and how bad at its worst?
reply: Right now, it's about a seven when I move or roll over. If I keep still, it's maybe a three.

utterance: Before I suggest a medicine: do you have any history of stomach ulcers, heartburn or bleeding from the stomach, any kidney problems, or asthma that gets worse with ibuprofen or aspirin?
reply: No, I don't have any history of stomach ulcers or heartburn that gets worse with anti-inflammatories, but I do have asthma. My kidneys are fine as far as I know.

awards.label: Stomach ulcers or indigestion with anti-inflammatories
Kidney problems
Asthma

utterance: Are you taking any other medicines, including anything from the chemist, herbal or supplements?
reply: I'm not taking anything else. I've got an allergy to tramadol, which causes vomiting and dizziness, but that's it.

utterance: Have you ever taken ibuprofen, aspirin or similar anti-inflammatories before, and did they ever bring on wheeze or make your asthma worse?
reply: No, I haven't taken ibuprofen, aspirin or similar medicines before. I know I'm allergic to tramadol, but I haven't had any issues with anti-inflammatories.

awards.label: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally three times daily with food, short course

utterance: Good news: your examination shows no signs of any nerve damage or anything serious. This is almost certainly a muscle and ligament strain in your lower back from the lifting. That's very common and it heals well on its own, usually over two to six weeks.
reply: I'm relieved to hear there's nothing serious, but I'm still worried it might be something more. I just want to make sure I'm not missing anything.

utterance: I know you came in wanting an MRI, but for back pain like yours — no leg weakness, no numbness, no bladder or bowel problems, and no fever or other warning signs — a scan doesn't help and isn't needed right now. An MRI often shows normal age-related changes that can worry you without changing the treatment, and it won't make you recover faster. So I'd suggest we hold off on the scan.
reply: I understand that a scan isn't needed right now. I just want to make sure I'm not missing anything, but I'll go with your assessment.

utterance: The most important treatment is to keep gently active and avoid staying in bed. Lying still too long actually makes things worse. Do your normal daily activities as much as you can, but avoid heavy lifting and anything that sharply increases the pain for the next few weeks. A heat pack on the sore area is fine.
reply: I'll try to keep moving and avoid heavy lifting. I'll use the heat pack as you suggested. I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything that could make it worse.

utterance: For the pain, I've prescribed ibuprofen 400 mg to take three times a day with food, for five days. Because you have asthma, stop it and contact me if you get any wheeze, tight chest or stomach pain. You can keep using paracetamol between doses if helpful, but don't take more than the pack says.
reply: I'll take the ibuprofen as prescribed, but I'll keep an eye on how I feel. I'll stop it straight away if I get any wheeze or tightness in my chest.

utterance: One more important thing: please come back or go to the emergency department straight away if you develop any of these — new numbness around your bottom or between your legs, difficulty passing urine or loss of bladder or bowel control, new weakness in a leg or foot, or pain going right down into your leg.
reply: I'll make sure to come back or go to the ED if any of those things happen. I'll keep an eye out for any new symptoms.

utterance: Also see me again if the pain isn't clearly improving within about two to three weeks, or sooner if you get a fever, feel generally unwell, or the pain suddenly becomes much worse at rest or at night. If it hasn't settled by around six weeks, then we can reconsider whether a scan or other tests are needed.
reply: I'll keep an eye on how I'm feeling and come back if it's not getting better. I'll make sure to mention anything new if it happens.

utterance: You can continue working from home but try to change position regularly and take short walks. Would you like me to arrange a review appointment in a couple of weeks, or would you prefer to book if it's not settling?
reply: I'd prefer to book a review if it's not settling. I'll let you know if anything changes.

awards.label: Correct diagnosis: Acute non-specific low back pain
Reasonable differential: Lumbar disc prolapse with sciatica
Reasonable differential: Cauda equina syndrome
Can't-miss diagnosis considered: Cauda equina syndrome
